Thumbless — Privacy Policy

Last updated: 2026-09-03

Thumbless ("the Product", "we") is a browser extension that plays the next short video by itself after the current one finishes. This policy explains exactly what data the Product does and does not handle.

It is written to be checkable against the package you installed. Every capability below is scoped to the build that actually has it, and §3 lists the literal contents of the shipped manifest so you — or a store reviewer — can unzip the extension and compare.

1. Which build this describes

EditionHow you can tell which one you haveStatus today
Trial editionNo sign-in, no licence-key field, no checkout. The options page shows a free-trial countdown and a price list with checkout marked as "not open yet".The only edition published
Subscription editionThe same product plus a licence-key field and an account sign-in on the options page, so a purchase can be activated.Not published

Where a section below says "in the subscription edition", that capability is absent from the trial edition. Absent, not merely switched off: the trial build declares no host permission for any server of ours, and an extension cannot reach a server it holds no host permission for.

When the subscription edition is published, this policy is updated before that build ships, and the store listing's data-collection declarations are updated with it.

2. The one-line version

Thumbless advances to the next short video after the current one finishes. It does not collect your browsing history, does not read or transmit page content, and never performs any social action (no likes, comments, follows, shares, or messages).

In the published trial edition, nothing at all leaves your device. There is no account, no server, and no telemetry destination.

3. What the published trial edition declares

These are the literal contents of the shipped package's manifest.json:

  • Permissions: storage, activeTab, scripting — and nothing else.

    • storage keeps your settings and the small local state listed below.
    • activeTab lets the popup read the address of the one tab you are looking at, only when you click the toolbar icon, so it can say whether that page has a video feed. It does not grant access to any other tab, and it grants nothing when the popup is closed.
    • scripting starts the engine on a site you have just turned on, and registers it so your choice survives a reload. It is only ever used for sites you explicitly granted.
  • Sites the extension runs on automatically (content-script matches): www.youtube.com, m.youtube.com, www.tiktok.com, www.instagram.com, *.facebook.com, www.snapchat.com, www.reddit.com, sh.reddit.com, x.com, twitter.com, www.threads.net, www.threads.com. On these sites the content script loads but stays inert until you turn the engine on and a short-video feed is actually on screen.
  • **Optional permission — any site (*://*/*), requested one site at a time.** This is declared as optional, which means the browser grants nothing at install and shows no warning for it. It is requested only when you press "Turn on here" on a site that is not in the list above; the browser then asks you about that one named site. Removing the site in the extension's settings hands the permission straight back to the browser, and revoking it in the browser's own extension settings is honoured immediately.
  • Not requested: alarms, tabs, history, webRequest, cookies, downloads, <all_urls> at install, and any host permission for a server of ours.
  • No remote code. Everything that runs is inside the package you installed.
  • No network activity. The trial edition contains no server address and makes no requests.

What storage holds in this edition:

Stored locallyWhy
Your settings — on/off, completion threshold, grace delay, per-feed switches, sleep timer, accessibility optionsTo apply your preferences. Kept in the browser's synced extension storage, so if your browser profile syncs, your settings follow it — the same mechanism every extension's preferences use.
A randomly generated install idTo keep per-install state stable. In this edition it is never transmitted, because there is nowhere to transmit it to.
The date the free trial started, and a "latest time seen" markTo know when the trial ends, and to stop a wound-back system clock from restarting it.
The list of sites you turned on by hand — host names only, never full addressesSo "Turn on here" survives a reload. A host name cannot record where on a site you have been.

The policy audit log (§8) is kept in memory for the tab only and is not written to storage.

4. What the Product accesses, and whether it leaves your device

Data / capabilityWhyLeaves your device?
The DOM of a short-video page on a site listed in §3, or a site you turned onTo find the video being watched, notice when it finishes, and move to the next oneNo — processed in the content script, on your machine, and never sent anywhere
The address of the active tab, only while the popup is openSo the popup can say whether this page has a feed and offer "Turn on here"No — read from the browser and used on the spot
Your settingsTo apply your preferencesNo in the trial edition. In the subscription edition, only if you sign in and turn settings sync on.
The install idStable per-install stateNo in the trial edition. In the subscription edition it accompanies licence-verification requests (§7).
Battery charging state, only if you turn on "Only while charging"To pause automation when you are not on powerNo — read from the browser and used on the spot
A licence key and an email address — subscription edition onlyTo activate a purchaseYes, to our own server, in that edition only (§7)

5. What the Product never does, in any edition

  • It never records or transmits the content of videos, pages, captions, comments, or your identity on any platform.
  • It never collects your browsing history. The content script loads only on the sites in §3 and on sites you turned on yourself, and it stays inert everywhere else. Only host names of sites you turned on are stored — never page addresses.
  • It never performs engagement actions. A policy guard permits exactly one category of action, "advance to the next item"; likes, comments, follows, shares, saves and messages are structurally unreachable in the code, not merely disabled. On a site you turned on yourself, the engine additionally refuses any control whose label suggests engagement, purchase or sign-in, and any link that would leave the site.
  • It never sells or shares personal data with third parties for advertising, and it contains no advertising or analytics SDK of any kind.

6. Reliability telemetry

The published trial edition sends no telemetry. No telemetry endpoint exists in it and it holds no host permission that would let it reach one; events are discarded before they reach the network. The switch in the options page is off by default and, in this edition, has nothing to send to even when on.

In the subscription edition, and only after you turn telemetry on, the Product may send content-free reliability events — for example "a video completed", "navigation succeeded or failed", "this feed's layout changed" — tagged with the install id and the feed name (youtube-shorts, tiktok-web, …). A sanitizer removes any field that could carry content — URLs, titles, video ids, free text, handles — before anything is sent. The purpose is narrow: to notice when a site changes its markup and the Product stops working there.

7. Accounts, purchases and retention — subscription edition only

The trial edition has no accounts and no payments. It collects no email address, because there is nothing to sign in to, and it cannot take money. The prices shown in the options page are information only.

In the subscription edition, activating a purchase stores your email address, a salted password hash, your subscription status, and — if you enable sync — your settings, on our server. You can delete the account and its data from the app, or by emailing the address in §11; deletion removes the account record and the synced settings.

Payments, in that edition, are taken by an external merchant of record on their own hosted checkout page. We never see or store card numbers. The payment provider receives whatever the transaction requires — typically your email address and billing country — under their own privacy policy, and is responsible for that data for invoicing and tax purposes.

Retention: account records are kept for as long as the account exists. Telemetry, where enabled, is retained in aggregate and is not linked to an account.

8. Local audit log

The Product keeps a local, in-memory log of every action the automation proposed — all of which are "advance to the next item" — and of anything the policy guard rejected. You can open it from the popup on any feed and copy it as JSON. It never leaves your device unless you explicitly copy it, and it is discarded when the tab closes. It exists so that you can verify, yourself, that nothing but navigation ever happened.

9. Other platforms

The browser extension is the only published product. Android, Android TV and Safari builds exist in the source tree but are not published, so nothing about them applies to anyone today.

If and when they are published, this policy will be updated before release, and in particular:

  • Android would use an Accessibility Service, narrowly, to detect the active short-video view and dispatch a single "next" gesture — with a prominent in-app disclosure, explicit user enablement, and no reading of screen content for any other purpose.
  • iOS / Safari would be a Safari Web Extension limited to the same supported websites, with no cross-app access.

10. Children

The Product is not a service directed at children, and it does not knowingly collect personal information from children. In the trial edition it collects no personal information from anyone.

11. Changes and contact
